concerns.text: Task T014 (tokenize_and_stream.py) depends on T013 (download_micro_corpus.py), but T013 is marked [P] (parallel-safe). T013 produces the raw data stream/file that T014 consumes. If T013 and T014 run in parallel, T014 will fail to find the input artifact. The [P] tag on T013 is incorrect if it implies it can run concurrently with its consumer T014, or the dependency chain is broken. T013 must complete before T014 starts.

Task T016 (split_data.py) depends on T015 (validate_corpus.py). T015 generates `corpus_validation.json` and validates the token count. T016 splits `micro_corpus_full.jsonl`. While T016 depends on the *file* produced by T014, the task description explicitly states 'Depends on: T015 (must pass validation before splitting)'. This is a valid logical dependency, but T015 is marked [P] (parallel-safe) in the list (T015 [US1]...), which is semantically incorrect if T015 is a gatekeeper that must finish before T016 starts. T015 cannot be parallel with T016.

Task T025 (run_experiment.py) depends on T018 (HumanEval exclusion verification). T018 is listed as a separate task in Phase 3. However, T018 is marked [US1] and T025 is [US2]. The dependency is valid (data hygiene before training), but T018 is not marked as a blocking prerequisite in the 'Phase Dependencies' section explicitly, though it is in the task description. More critically, T018 is marked [P] in the list? No, T018 is not marked [P]. But T017 is [P]. The issue is T025 depends on T018, but T018 is part of US1. If US1 and US2 run in parallel (as suggested in 'Parallel Opportunities'), T025 will start before T018 completes. The 'Parallel Opportunities' section claims 'All user stories can start in parallel', which violates the T025 -> T018 dependency.

Task T031 (compute_metrics.py) depends on T032 (evaluate_human_eval.py) and T023 (train_loop.py). T032 depends on T025.2 (checkpoint saving). T025.2 depends on T025. T025 depends on T018. The chain is long. However, T031 is marked [US3]. T032 is [US3]. T023 is [US2]. The dependency T031 -> T023 is valid (needs training logs). But T031 -> T032 -> T025.2 -> T025 -> T018. If US2 and US3 run in parallel, T031 will fail. The 'Parallel Opportunities' section states 'Different user stories can be worked on in parallel', which is false for US3 tasks that depend on US2 outputs (T031 depends on T023/T025).

Task T010 (Setup state file mechanism) is marked [P]. However, it is a foundational task that likely needs to be completed before any artifacts are generated to ensure they are hashed correctly (Constitution Principle V). If T010 runs in parallel with T001-T009, it might miss the initial state setup. It should be ordered before any artifact-producing tasks, not just marked [P].
